claim: The pro-inflammatory microenvironment during post-partum mammary involution promotes parity-associated breast cancer.
source: There is strong evidence that the pro-inflammatory microenvironment during post-partum mammary involution promotes parity-associated breast cancer.
evidence: This is stated as established evidence in the abstract and introduction, drawing from existing scientific understanding.

claim: Estrogen exposure during mammary involution drives tumor growth through neutrophils' activity.
source: Estrogen exposure during mammary involution drives tumor growth through neutrophils' activity.
evidence: This is stated as a known finding in the abstract, referencing prior work.

claim: 88% of estrogen-regulated genes in mammary tissue were mediated through neutrophils.
source: Remarkably, 88% of estrogen-regulated genes in mammary tissue were mediated through neutrophils, which were recruited through estrogen-induced CXCR2 signalling in an autocrine fashion.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis showing that neutrophil depletion eliminated 88% of estrogen-regulated genes.

claim: Neutrophils were recruited through estrogen-induced CXCR2 signalling in an autocrine fashion.
source: Remarkably, 88% of estrogen-regulated genes in mammary tissue were mediated through neutrophils, which were recruited through estrogen-induced CXCR2 signalling in an autocrine fashion.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing CXCR2 antagonist reduced neutrophil infiltration and estrogen upregulated CXCR2 and its ligands in neutrophils.

claim: Neutrophils mediate estrogen-induced inflammation and adipocytes repopulation.
source: While neutrophils mediate estrogen-induced inflammation and adipocytes repopulation, estrogen-induced mammary cell death was via lysosome-mediated programmed cell death through upregulation of cathepsin B, Tnf and Bid in a neutrophil-independent manner.
evidence: This is supported by neutrophil depletion experiments showing attenuation of inflammation and adipocyte repopulation.

claim: Estrogen-induced mammary cell death was via lysosome-mediated programmed cell death through upregulation of cathepsin B, Tnf and Bid in a neutrophil-independent manner.
source: While neutrophils mediate estrogen-induced inflammation and adipocytes repopulation, estrogen-induced mammary cell death was via lysosome-mediated programmed cell death through upregulation of cathepsin B, Tnf and Bid in a neutrophil-independent manner.
evidence: This is supported by data showing estrogen increased cathepsin B, Tnf, and Bid expression and neutrophil depletion did not affect estrogen-induced cell death.

claim: The multifaceted effects of estrogen are mostly mediated by ERα and unique to the phase of mammary involution.
source: Notably, these multifaceted effects of estrogen are mostly mediated by ERα and unique to the phase of mammary involution.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with ERα-specific agonist PPT and comparison with nulliparous mice.

claim: High levels of tissue fibrillar collagen and elevated expression of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) in the mammary gland drive tumor growth and lymph angiogenesis.
source: High levels of tissue fibrillar collagen and elevated expression of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) in the mammary gland have been shown to drive tumor growth and lymph angiogenesis (Lyons et al., 2014; Lyons et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Wound healing-like tissue environment associated with mammary involution promotes tumor development and dissemination.
source: Wound healing-like tissue environment associated with mammary involution is also known to promote tumor development and dissemination (Foster et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Estrogen has been shown to stimulate the growth of estrogen receptor-negative mammary tumors during mammary involution.
source: Estrogen has been shown to stimulate the growth of estrogen receptor-negative mammary tumors during mammary involution and estrogen-stimulated neutrophil activity plays a crucial role in fostering the pro-tumoral microenvironment (Chung et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Estrogen-stimulated neutrophil activity plays a crucial role in fostering the pro-tumoral microenvironment during mammary involution.
source: Estrogen has been shown to stimulate the growth of estrogen receptor-negative mammary tumors during mammary involution and estrogen-stimulated neutrophil activity plays a crucial role in fostering the pro-tumoral microenvironment (Chung et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Estrogen exposure during post-weaning mammary involution is a risk factor for parity-associated breast cancer.
source: This suggests that estrogen exposure during post-weaning mammary involution is a risk factor for parity-associated breast cancer.
evidence: This is inferred from the evidence that estrogen stimulates tumor growth during involution.

claim: The first phase of mammary involution is the reversible phase whereby the reintroduction of the pups within 48 hr can re-initiate lactation.
source: In mice, the first phase is the reversible phase whereby the reintroduction of the pups within 48 hr can re-initiate lactation (Li et al., 1997; Jaggi et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The first phase of mammary involution is typified by a decrease in milk protein synthesis and increased mammary cell death resulting in the appearance of shed, dying cells within the lumen of the distended alveoli.
source: It is typified by a decrease in milk protein synthesis and increased mammary cell death resulting in the appearance of shed, dying cells within the lumen of the distended alveoli (Strange et al., 1992; Walker et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Inflammation occurs in the first phase of mammary involution with the infiltration of immune cells and up-regulation of immune response genes.
source: Inflammation also occurs in the first phase with the infiltration of immune cells and up-regulation of immune response genes (Stein et al., 2004; Clarkson and Watson, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The second, and irreversible phase of mammary involution occurs after 72 hr of weaning.
source: The second, and irreversible phase of mammary involution occurs after 72 hr of weaning.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about mammary involution.

claim: The second phase of mammary involution is morphologically characterized by the collapse of the alveolar structure, the second wave of epithelial cell death, continued inflammation and the repopulation of adipocytes.
source: This phase is morphologically characterized by the collapse of the alveolar structure, the second wave of epithelial cell death, continued inflammation and the repopulation of adipocytes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about mammary involution.

claim: Tumor-associated neutrophils have been classified into the anti-tumor neutrophils (N1) and pro-tumor neutrophils (N2) based on the expression of specific markers.
source: Tumor-associated neutrophils have been classified into the anti-tumor neutrophils (N1) and pro-tumor neutrophils (N2) based on the expression of specific markers (Fridlender et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: A high circulating neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio is known as a strong biomarker of poor prognosis in various cancers.
source: Neutrophils are known to accumulate in the peripheral blood of patients with cancer and a high circulating neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio is known as a strong biomarker of poor prognosis in various cancers (Shaul and Fridlender, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Circulating neutrophils in mice model can be classified into the low-density and high-density neutrophils (LDN and HDN).
source: Based on density gradient centrifugation, circulating neutrophils in mice model can also be classified into the low-density and high-density neutrophils (LDN and HDN) (Sagiv et al., 2015; Mishalian et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: LDN was associated with immunosuppressive activity promoting tumor growth while HDN was considered cytotoxic to the tumor.
source: LDN was associated with immunosuppressive activity promoting tumor growth while HDN was considered cytotoxic to the tumor.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous research.

claim: Neutrophils were reported to be the first immune cells recruited into mammary tissue during involution.
source: Neutrophils were reported to be the first immune cells recruited into mammary tissue during involution (Stein et al., 2004), although the significance of their presence is not known.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Estrogen treatment retards mammary involution in mice based on histological examination.
source: In mice, a histological examination in 1970 reported that estrogen treatment retards mammary involution (Satoh, 1970).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Estrogen was reported to promote the regression of mammary glands in rats by up-regulating a 60K gelatinase which degrades collagen and participate in extracellular matrix remodelling.
source: However, estrogen was reported to promote the regression of mammary glands in rats by up-regulating a 60K gelatinase which degrades collagen and participate in extracellular matrix remodelling (Ambili et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Injection of estrogen during the dry off period in dairy cows hastened involution based on the abrupt decline of milk synthesis and secretion.
source: Similar to the observation in rats, injection of estrogen during the dry off period in dairy cows hastened involution based on the abrupt decline of milk synthesis and secretion (Athie et al., 1997; Athie et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: E2B caused significantly more mammary cell death, as evidenced by the increase of the number of shed cells with hyper-condensed nuclei in the lumen.
source: E2B caused significantly more mammary cell death, as evidenced by the increase of the number of shed cells with hyper-condensed nuclei in the lumen, a characteristic of programmed cell death (Figure 1, Ai, and 1B, p=0.0131).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis and quantification shown in Figure 1.

claim: E2B significantly increased the number of cleaved caspase-3-positive (CC3+) mammary cells.
source: This effect was associated with an increase in the number of cleaved caspase-3-positive (CC3+) mammary cells (Figure 1, Aii, and 1B, p=0.0283).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: E2B significantly increased the repopulation of adipocytes based on the staining of perilipin.
source: E2B also significantly increased the repopulation of adipocytes based on the staining of perilipin, a lipid droplet-associated protein (Greenberg et al., 1991; Figure 1, Aiii, and 1B, p=0.0155).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Perilipin is a lipid droplet-associated protein.
source: E2B also significantly increased the repopulation of adipocytes based on the staining of perilipin, a lipid droplet-associated protein (Greenberg et al., 1991; Figure 1, Aiii, and 1B, p=0.0155).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: E2B decreased the expression of milk proteins β-casein (Csn2).
source: Accordingly, E2B decreased the expression of milk proteins β-casein (Csn2) (Figure 1C, p=0.0187).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Stromelysin-1 (Mmp3) gene deletion or Timp1 overexpression in mice accelerated mammary adipogenesis.
source: In particular, stromelysin-1 (Mmp3) gene deletion or Timp1 overexpression in mice accelerated mammary adipogenesis (Barker et al., 2011; Alexander et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: E2B-induced adipocyte repopulation was associated with increases in the gene expression of Timp1, Mmp3 and Mmp9, but decrease in the expression of Timp2.
source: Intriguingly, E2B-induced adipocyte repopulation was associated with increases in the gene expression of Timp1, Mmp3 and Mmp9, but decrease in the expression of Timp2.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The ratio of Mmp3 to Timp1 did not change in response to E2B.
source: However, the ratio of Mmp3 to Timp1 did not change in response to E2B (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Estrogen increased mammary neutrophils significantly.
source: Figure 1Di shows that estrogen increased mammary neutrophils significantly (p=0.0002).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1Di.

claim: Ly6G antibody reduced neutrophils in the mammary tissue of E2B-treated samples by ~90%.
source: Ly6G antibody reduced neutrophils in the mammary tissue of E2B-treated samples by ~90%.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1Di.

claim: Neutrophil depletion had no effect on E2B-induced mammary cell death.
source: Interestingly, whilst neutrophil depletion had no effect on E2B-induced mammary cell death, it attenuated E2B-induced adipocytes repopulation (Figure 1Dii).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 1Dii and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Neutrophil depletion attenuated E2B-induced adipocytes repopulation.
source: Interestingly, whilst neutrophil depletion had no effect on E2B-induced mammary cell death, it attenuated E2B-induced adipocytes repopulation (Figure 1Dii).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 1Dii and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Neutrophils are critical for estrogen-induced inflammation and adipocytes repopulation, but not for mammary cell death.
source: Taken together, we conclude that estrogen promotes mammary involution, and neutrophils are critical for estrogen-induced inflammation and adipocytes repopulation, but not for mammary cell death.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on neutrophil depletion effects.

claim: A total of 1987 genes were significantly (padj < 0.05) regulated by E2B in IgG groups with very high fold changes.
source: As shown in the volcano plot (Figure 2A, top panel), a total of 1987 genes were significantly (padj < 0.05) regulated by E2B in IgG groups with very high fold changes (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: Of the E2B-regulated genes, 513 genes were up-regulated, and 148 genes were down-regulated with a fold change ≥ 2.
source: Of these genes, 513 genes were up-regulated, and 148 genes were down-regulated with a fold change ≥ 2 (Figure 2A, top panel).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Estrogen regulates genes involved in diverse biological processes including leukocyte migration, regulation of inflammatory response, and cytokine-mediated signalling.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis showed that estrogen regulates genes involved in diverse biological processes (Figure 2C). Leukocyte migration, regulation of inflammatory response, and cytokine-mediated signalling are among the top biological processes regulated.
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis of RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: E2B also regulated genes in epithelial cell proliferation, cell death, and fat cell differentiation.
source: E2B also regulated genes in epithelial cell proliferation, cell death, and fat cell differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis of RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Neutrophil depletion eliminated 88% of estrogen-regulated genes.
source: Remarkably, neutrophil depletion eliminated 88% of estrogen-regulated genes (Figure 2B, top panel), that is, 1746 out of 1987 E2B-regulated genes in mammary tissue were regulated in neutrophils directly, or indirectly through the activities of neutrophils.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis comparing IgG and Ly6G groups shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 12% (241 genes) of E2B-regulated genes in mammary tissue are independent of neutrophils.
source: Correspondingly, 12% (241 genes) of E2B-regulated genes in mammary tissue are independent of neutrophils.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There is only one differentially regulated gene (padj < 0.05) between IgG and Ly6G groups in the absence of estrogen.
source: It is also noteworthy that there is only one differentially regulated gene (padj < 0.05) between IgG and Ly6G groups in the absence of estrogen (Figure 2B, bottom panel).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: E2B-regulated GO terms including leukocyte migration, inflammatory response, cytokines and chemokines related pathways, and fat cell differentiation were all eliminated in neutrophil depleted samples.
source: Consistent with the function of neutrophils, E2B-regulated GO terms including leukocyte migration, inflammatory response, cytokines and chemokines related pathways, and fat cell differentiation were all eliminated in neutrophil depleted samples (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis of RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: GO terms such as epithelial cell proliferation and developmental growth persisted in neutrophil-depleted samples, suggesting that their stimulation by E2B are independent of neutrophils.
source: On the other hand, GO terms such as epithelial cell proliferation and developmental growth persisted in neutrophil-depleted samples, suggesting that their stimulation by E2B are independent of neutrophils (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis of RNA-Seq data shown in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: 63 E2B-regulated genes with fold change ≥ 3 were associated with leukocyte migration and inflammation.
source: Based on the GO over-representation analysis, 63 E2B-regulated genes with fold change ≥ 3 were associated with leukocyte migration and inflammation (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis of RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: All 63 genes associated with leukocyte migration and inflammation were no longer E2B-regulated after neutrophil depletion.
source: All 63 genes were no longer E2B-regulated after neutrophil depletion (in Ly6G group).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis comparing IgG and Ly6G groups shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Acod1, Trem1, Trem3, and Il1b are among the top up-regulated genes based on fold induction.
source: Aconitate decarboxylase 1 (Acod1), triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 1 (Trem1), triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 3 (Trem3), and interleukin one beta (Il1b) are among the top up-regulated genes based on fold induction.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Mirt2 is a lipopolysaccharides (LPS)-induced long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) in macrophages and was reported to be a negative regulator of LPS-induced inflammation both in vivo and in vitro.
source: Mirt2 is a lipopolysaccharides (LPS)-induced long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) in macrophages and was reported to be a negative regulator of LPS-induced inflammation both in vivo and in vitro (Du et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Mirt2 upregulation by E2B in neutrophils indicates its involvement in the moderation of estrogen-induced inflammatory response during mammary involution.
source: Thus, Mirt2 upregulation by E2B in neutrophils indicates its involvement in the moderation of estrogen-induced inflammatory response during mammary involution.
evidence: This is inferred from the known function of Mirt2 and its upregulation by E2B.

claim: S100a8 and S100a9 were all induced by E2B in neutrophils.
source: Consistent with a previous report (Chung et al., 2017), S100 calcium-binding protein A8 (S100a8) and A9 (S100a9) were all induced by E2B in neutrophils and validated by qPCR (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq and qPCR data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Cxcr2 and its known ligands Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Cxcl3 and Cxcl5 were all upregulated by E2B.
source: More interestingly, C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 2 (Cxcr2) and its known ligands in the mouse (Bachelerie et al., 2019), C-X-C motif chemokine ligand Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Cxcl3 and Cxcl5 were all upregulated by E2B (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Estrogen upregulated the expression of Cxcr2, Cxcl2, Cxcl3 and Cxcl5 in Dynabeads-isolated neutrophils.
source: Furthermore, qPCR analysis verified that estrogen upregulated the expression of Cxcr2, Cxcl2, Cxcl3 and Cxcl5 in Dynabeads-isolated neutrophils (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data on isolated neutrophils shown in Figure 3B.

claim: S100A8 and S100A9 are known neutrophil chemoattractants that promote neutrophil migration during inflammation.
source: S100A8, S100A9 are known neutrophil chemoattractants that promote neutrophil migration during inflammation (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: S100A8 and S100A9 are small calcium-binding proteins that activate calcium-dependent signalling through receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE) or toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4).
source: S100A8 and S100A9 are small calcium-binding proteins that activate calcium-dependent signalling through receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE) or toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about S100A8/A9 function.

claim: Paquinimod (PAQ) is a derivative of quinoline-3-carboxamide that has been shown to inhibit S100A9 activity through binding with S100A9.
source: Paquinimod (PAQ) is a derivative of quinoline-3-carboxamide that has been shown to inhibit S100A9 activity through binding with S100A9 (Bengtsson et al., 2012; Björk et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The binding of PAQ to S100A9 inhibits S100A9 dimerization or the formation of heterodimer with S100A8, thereby preventing the activation of RAGE or TLR4.
source: The binding inhibits S100A9 dimerization or the formation of heterodimer with S100A8, thereby preventing the activation of RAGE or TLR4.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about PAQ mechanism of action.

claim: E2B+PAQ treatment resulted in an increase in mammary neutrophils when compared to E2B treated samples.
source: Flow cytometry analysis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) showed that E2B+PAQ treatment resulted in an increase in mammary neutrophils (CD45+ CD11b+ Ly6G+, p=0.0238) and monocytes (CD45+ CD11b+ Ly6Chi, p=0.0242) when compared to E2B treated samples.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: E2B+PAQ treatment resulted in an increase in mammary monocytes when compared to E2B treated samples.
source: Flow cytometry analysis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) showed that E2B+PAQ treatment resulted in an increase in mammary neutrophils (CD45+ CD11b+ Ly6G+, p=0.0238) and monocytes (CD45+ CD11b+ Ly6Chi, p=0.0242) when compared to E2B treated samples.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CXCR2 is known to be important for neutrophil infiltration in a number of experimental settings.
source: CXCR2 is known to be important for neutrophil infiltration in a number of experimental settings (Aziz et al., 2012; Alves-Filho et al., 2010; Cacalano et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: E2B treatment alone without the antagonist led to 2.57-fold increase in mammary neutrophils as compared to the Ctrl+DMSO.
source: As shown in Figure 3Ci, E2B treatment alone without the antagonist (E2B+DMSO) led to 2.57-fold increase (p=0.0082) in mammary neutrophils as compared to the Ctrl+DMSO.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3Ci.

claim: E2B+SB225002 treatment caused a 2.26-fold reduction in mammary neutrophils when compared to the E2B+DMSO group.
source: E2B+SB225002 treatment caused a 2.26-fold reduction in mammary neutrophils when compared to the E2B+DMSO group (p=0.0508).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3Ci.

claim: SB225002 significantly reduced the number of infiltrated mammary neutrophils within a 20 mm2 area of stained mammary tissue.
source: Quantification of the number of infiltrated mammary neutrophils within a 20 mm2 area of stained mammary tissue also showed a significant reduction of neutrophil infiltration within mammary tissue (Figure 3Cii, p=0.0369).
evidence: This is supported by histological quantification shown in Figure 3Cii.

claim: The E2B-induced pro-inflammatory markers such as Cxcl2, S100a9, Clec4d, and Clec4e were all significantly reduced with E2B+SB225002 treatment compared with E2B+DMSO treatment.
source: qPCR analysis of the mammary tissue samples showed that the E2B-induced pro-inflammatory markers such as Cxcl2, S100a9, Clec4d, and Clec4e were all significantly reduced with E2B+SB225002 treatment compared with E2B+DMSO treatment (Figure 3D, Cxcl2, p=0.0279; S100a9, p=0.0199; Clec4d, p=0.0051; Clec4e, p=0.0183).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The E2B-induced activation of CXCR2 signalling and the up-regulation of CXCR2 ligands Cxcl2, Cxcl3, Cxcl5 in neutrophils plays a pivotal role in estrogen-induced neutrophil recruitment.
source: Collectively, the data showed that the E2B-induced activation of CXCR2 signalling and the up-regulation of CXCR2 ligands Cxcl2, Cxcl3, Cxcl5 in neutrophils plays a pivotal role in estrogen-induced neutrophil recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the CXCR2 inhibitor experiments and gene expression data.

claim: Neutrophil depletion efficiency at INV D3 and D4 were ~ 95%.
source: Neutrophil depletion efficiency at INV D3 and D4 were ~ 95%.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The infiltrated neutrophils at INV D4 is ~ 8 times of that at D3.
source: It was also shown that the infiltrated neutrophils at INV D4 is ~ 8 times of that at D3 (Figure 4A), indicating an increase of infiltrated neutrophils as involution proceeded.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Neutrophils depletion reduced mammary monocytes at both D3 and D4, although it is statistically not significant.
source: In our study, neutrophils depletion also reduced mammary monocytes at both D3 and D4, although it is statistically not significant (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: At INV D3, neutrophil depletion showed no effect on adipocytes repopulation.
source: At INV D3, neutrophil depletion showed no effect on adipocytes repopulation (Figure 4C, p=0.3737 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by perilipin immunostaining data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was a significant reduction in adipocytes repopulation with neutrophil depletion at INV D4 based on perilipin immunostaining.
source: However, there was a significant reduction in adipocytes repopulation with neutrophil depletion at INV D4 based on perilipin immunostaining (Figure 4C, p=0.0077, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by perilipin immunostaining data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Neutrophils involvement in adipocytes repopulation during mammary involution is limited to a specific time window when the levels of neutrophil infiltration is high.
source: The data suggest that neutrophils involvement in adipocytes repopulation during mammary involution is limited to a specific time window when the levels of neutrophil infiltration is high.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that neutrophil depletion only affected adipocyte repopulation at INV D4 but not D3.

claim: E2B down-regulated the expression of Adipoq, Pparg, and Lpl independent of neutrophils, all of which are positive regulators of adipogenesis.
source: For example, E2B down-regulated the expression of Adipoq, Pparg, and Lpl independent of neutrophils, all of which are positive regulators of adipogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: E2B up-regulated some of the upstream regulators of adipogenesis, such as Egr2, Adig, Cebpb, and Cebpd.
source: On the other hand, E2B also up-regulated some of the upstream regulators of adipogenesis, such as early growth response 2 (Egr2), adipogenin (Adig), CCAAT/enhancer binding protein (C/EBP), beta (Cebpb), and CCAAT/enhancer binding protein (C/EBP), delta (Cebpd), all of which were validated by qPCR analysis (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq and qPCR data shown in Figures 4D and 4E.

claim: Neutrophil depletion abolished the up-regulation of Egr2, Adig and Cebp/b.
source: Neutrophil depletion abolished the up-regulation of Egr2, Adig and Cebp/b.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Although Cebpb and Cebpd are no longer upregulated by E2B in neutrophils depleted samples, the relative expressions of Cebpb and Cebpd were increased upon neutrophil depletion.
source: Interestingly, although Cebpb and Cebpd are no longer upregulated by E2B in neutrophils depleted samples, the relative expressions of Cebpb and Cebpd were increased upon neutrophil depletion (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Neutrophils depletion exerted positive influence on the expression of Cebpb and Cebpd in mammary tissue.
source: This seems to suggest that neutrophils depletion exerted positive influence on the expression of Cebpb and Cebpd in mammary tissue and this would limit a further increase in response to E2B.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Cebpb and Cebpd expression increased with neutrophil depletion.

claim: Macrophages have been shown to be critical for adipocytes repopulation during mammary involution.
source: First, macrophages have been shown to be critical for adipocytes repopulation during mammary involution (O'Brien et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Estrogen has been reported to regulate gene expression of peritoneal macrophages involved in various processes including cell proliferation, immune response and wound healing.
source: Whilst we did not examine the effect of estrogen on mammary resident macrophages, estrogen has been reported to regulate gene expression of peritoneal macrophages involved in various processes including cell proliferation, immune response and wound healing (Pepe et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Estrogen induces infiltration of monocytes into mammary tissue.
source: Second, estrogen also induces infiltration of monocytes into mammary tissue (Chung et al., 2017), which share common properties with F4/80+ macrophages.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Estrogen-induced neutrophil depletion reduced, to a small extent, infiltrating monocytes.
source: Third, consistent with the understanding that infiltrated neutrophils recruit monocytes into the tissue during sterile inflammation (Shen et al., 2013), we observed that estrogen-induced neutrophil depletion reduced, to a small extent, infiltrating monocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Infiltrated neutrophils recruit monocytes into the tissue during sterile inflammation.
source: Third, consistent with the understanding that infiltrated neutrophils recruit monocytes into the tissue during sterile inflammation (Shen et al., 2013), we observed that estrogen-induced neutrophil depletion reduced, to a small extent, infiltrating monocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Estrogen-induced adipocytes repopulation is plausibly mediated by the activities of neutrophils, infiltrated monocytes as well as resident macrophages in the mammary gland.
source: Taken together, estrogen-induced adipocytes repopulation is plausibly mediated by the activities of neutrophils, infiltrated monocytes as well as resident macrophages in the mammary gland.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and cited literature.

claim: LM-PCD has been shown to be the major mechanism of mammary cell death in phase I of mammary involution, and it is independent of caspases 3, 6, and 7.
source: In phase I, LM-PCD has been shown to be the major mechanism of mammary cell death, and it is independent of caspases 3, 6, and 7 (Kreuzaler et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: STAT3 has been shown to be a regulator for LM-PCD during involution by inducing the expression of lysosomal proteases cathepsin B (CTSB) and L (CTSL), while down-regulating their endogenous inhibitor Spi2A.
source: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) has been shown to be a regulator for LM-PCD during involution by inducing the expression of lysosomal proteases cathepsin B (CTSB) and L (CTSL), while down-regulating their endogenous inhibitor Spi2A (Kreuzaler et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Estrogen significantly enhanced cell death during the acute phase of mammary involution.
source: Despite its well-known function in stimulating mammary growth, estrogen significantly enhanced cell death during the acute phase of mammary involution (Figure 1A and B, p<0.05).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: E2B up-regulated Ctsb expression.
source: Since both RNA-Seq analysis and qPCR demonstrated E2B up-regulation of Ctsb expression (Figure 5A, IgG, p=0.0163; Ly6G, p=0.0182, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), we evaluated the protein levels of cathepsins.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq and qPCR data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The pro and active form (sc, single-chain) of CTSB were significantly up-regulated in the E2B-treated mammary gland.
source: Indeed, the pro and active form (sc, single-chain) of CTSB were significantly up-regulated (pro-CTSB, p=0.0358; sc-CTSB, p=0.0101) in the E2B-treated mammary gland.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The sc-form of cathepsin D (CTSD) and CTSL were significantly up-regulated by E2B.
source: Furthermore, the sc-form of cathepsin D (CTSD) and CTSL were also significantly up-regulated by E2B (Figure 5B, sc-CTSD, p=0.0222; sc-CTSL, p=0.0385), although the levels of pro-CTSD and CTSL were unchanged.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: E2B had no effect on the expression of Ctsd and Ctsl.
source: Since E2B had no effect on the expression of Ctsd and Ctsl (data not shown), the increase of the sc-form of CTSD and CTSL can be explained by the up-regulation of CTSB which catalyses the removal of the N-terminal propeptide from itself and from CTSD and CTSL, leading to an increase in active forms of cathepsins B, D, and L (Mach et al., 1994; Ménard et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated based on data not shown in the manuscript.

claim: CTSB catalyses the removal of the N-terminal propeptide from itself and from CTSD and CTSL, leading to an increase in active forms of cathepsins B, D, and L.
source: Since E2B had no effect on the expression of Ctsd and Ctsl (data not shown), the increase of the sc-form of CTSD and CTSL can be explained by the up-regulation of CTSB which catalyses the removal of the N-terminal propeptide from itself and from CTSD and CTSL, leading to an increase in active forms of cathepsins B, D, and L (Mach et al., 1994; Ménard et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Neutrophil depletion had no effect on E2B-induced increase of active form of CTSB.
source: Consistent with the lack of neutrophil influence on E2B-induced cell death, neutrophil depletion had no effect on E2B-induced increase of active form of CTSB (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: E2B significantly induced the expression of tumor necrosis factor (Tnf).
source: E2B also significantly induced the expression of tumor necrosis factor (Tnf) (Figure 5A, IgG, p=0.0161; Ly6G, p=0.0343, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), which is a known upstream activator of STAT3.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: TNF is a known upstream activator of STAT3.
source: E2B also significantly induced the expression of tumor necrosis factor (Tnf) (Figure 5A, IgG, p=0.0161; Ly6G, p=0.0343, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), which is a known upstream activator of STAT3.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: E2B did not affect the levels of phosphorylated and total STAT3.
source: However, E2B did not affect the levels of phosphorylated and total STAT3 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The up-regulation of Ctsb expression by E2B is a direct event independent of STAT3 activation.
source: This suggests that the up-regulation of Ctsb expression by E2B is a direct event independent of STAT3 activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that E2B upregulated Ctsb but did not affect STAT3 phosphorylation.

claim: E2B up-regulated the expression of BH3 interacting domain death agonist (Bid), independent of neutrophils.
source: Furthermore, E2B also up-regulated the expression of BH3 interacting domain death agonist (Bid), independent of neutrophils (Figure 5A, IgG, p=0.0119; Ly6G, p=0.0248, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Bid is a well-established pro-apoptotic marker, and its overexpression has been reported to promote cell death.
source: Bid is a well-established pro-apoptotic marker, and its overexpression has been reported to promote cell death (Fukazawa et al., 2003; Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: E2B-induced increases of the sc-form of CTSB and CTSL occurred mostly in the cytosolic fraction.
source: Consistently, E2B-induced increases of the sc-form of CTSB and CTSL occurred mostly in the cytosolic fraction (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by subcellular fractionation data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: E2B promotes mammary cell death by increasing the activity of lysosomal proteases CTSB, CTSD, and CTSL under the cellular condition of mammary involution.
source: These findings further support the notion that E2B promotes mammary cell death by increasing the activity of lysosomal proteases CTSB, CTSD, and CTSL under the cellular condition of mammary involution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on cathepsin expression and localization.

claim: Wild-type MCF7 does not express caspase-3.
source: As wild-type MCF7 does not express caspase-3 (Jänicke, 2009), the hypothesis was tested in an in vitro model using MCF7-caspase3(+) breast cancer cell line (Jänicke et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Increasing concentration of TNFα from 2 ng/ml to 10 ng/ml led to a dose-dependent increase in the percentage of dead cells.
source: As shown in Figure 6A, increasing concentration of TNFα from 2 ng/ml to 10 ng/ml led to a dose-dependent increase in the percentage of dead cells (p<0.01).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: E2B treatment alone did not cause cell death in MCF7-caspase3(+) cells.
source: As expected, E2B treatment alone did not cause cell death.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: E2B+TNFα treatment significantly enhanced the percentage of dead cells compared to TNFα treatment alone at doses of 5 ng/ml and 10 ng/ml.
source: However, E2B+TNFα treatment significantly enhanced the percentage of dead cells compared to TNFα treatment alone at doses of 5 ng/ml (p=0.0104) and 10 ng/ml (p=0.0007).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: TNFα induced increases in p-STAT3 and cleaved poly-ADP ribose polymerase (PARP) protein as compared to the vehicle-treated controls.
source: Expectedly, TNFα induced increases in p-STAT3 and cleaved poly-ADP ribose polymerase (PARP) protein as compared to the vehicle-treated controls (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: E2B+TNFα increased the levels of p-STAT3 and cleaved PARP significantly compared to TNFα treatment alone.
source: E2B+TNFα increased the levels of p-STAT3 and cleaved PARP significantly compared to TNFα treatment alone (Figure 6B and C, p-STAT3, p=0.0404; cleaved PARP, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figures 6B and 6C.

claim: Pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNFα primes the death-inducing effect of estrogen.
source: Together, the in vitro data support the notion that pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNFα primes the death-inducing effect of estrogen.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vitro experiments with MCF7-caspase3(+) cells.

claim: Estrogen-induced cell death in the presence of TNFα may not be via LM-PCD in the MCF7-caspase3(+) cells.
source: However, the increased p-STAT3 is not associated with increases of active CTSD and CTSB (data not shown), suggesting that estrogen-induced cell death in the presence of TNFα may not be via LM-PCD in the MCF7-caspase3(+) cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that p-STAT3 increased but cathepsins did not.

claim: ERα-specific agonist PPT elicited similar changes as E2B on the expression of a panel of inflammatory and adipogenesis-related genes in neutrophil.
source: Secondly, ERα-specific agonist PPT elicited similar changes as E2B on the expression of a panel of inflammatory and adipogenesis-related genes in neutrophil (Figure 8).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 8.

claim: ERβ-specific agonist DPN had no effect on the expression of inflammatory and adipogenesis-related genes.
source: In contrast, ERβ-specific agonist DPN, had no effect.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 8.

claim: ERα has been reported to mediate estrogen-induced neutrophil migration in the uterus through ERα phosphorylation at serine 216.
source: ERα has also been reported to mediate estrogen-induced neutrophil migration in the uterus through ERα phosphorylation at serine 216 (Shindo et al., 2013), and ERα mediated the effect of estrogen on myeloid-derived suppressor cells, which are mostly granulocytic cells, in stimulating tumor development in mice model (Svoronos et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: ERα mediated the effect of estrogen on myeloid-derived suppressor cells in stimulating tumor development in mice model.
source: ERα has also been reported to mediate estrogen-induced neutrophil migration in the uterus through ERα phosphorylation at serine 216 (Shindo et al., 2013), and ERα mediated the effect of estrogen on myeloid-derived suppressor cells, which are mostly granulocytic cells, in stimulating tumor development in mice model (Svoronos et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: ERα plays a major part in mediating estrogen regulation of neutrophils activity during mammary involution.
source: Thus, ERα plays a major part in mediating estrogen regulation of neutrophils activity during mammary involution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data with ERα agonist and previous literature.

claim: Neutrophils undergo dynamic changes in their epigenome during development.
source: It has been reported that neutrophils undergo dynamic changes in their epigenome during development (Grassi et al., 2018; Rönnerblad et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Under mature state, neutrophils respond to environmental cues with epigenetic modification and transcription changes.
source: Under mature state, neutrophils respond to environmental cues with epigenetic modification and transcription changes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about neutrophil biology.

claim: The inactive IL-6 genomic locus in human neutrophils undergoes chromatin remodeling in response to ligands for TLR8, leading to IL-6 secretion.
source: For example, the inactive IL-6 genomic locus in human neutrophils undergoes chromatin remodeling in response to ligands for TLR8, leading to IL-6 secretion (Zimmermann et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: ERα cistrome is reprogrammable and TNFα has been shown to reshape the genomic action of estrogen in breast cancer cells through redistribution of NF-kB and pioneer factor FOXA1 binding across the genome.
source: It is known that ERα cistrome is reprogrammable and TNFα has been shown to reshape the genomic action of estrogen in breast cancer cells through redistribution of NF-kB and pioneer factor FOXA1 binding across the genome (Frasor et al., 2009; Franco et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The inflammatory microenvironment in mammary tissue during involution may trigger a global shift of ER-cistrome in mammary neutrophils so as to modify estrogen response that is distinct from that in nulliparous mice.
source: Thus, the inflammatory microenvironment in mammary tissue during involution may trigger a global shift of ER-cistrome in mammary neutrophils so as to modify estrogen response that is distinct from that in nulliparous mice.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the observed differences in estrogen response between involution and nulliparous states.

claim: Selective ERβ agonist LY500307 was found to reduce lung metastasis of triple-negative breast cancer cells.
source: Selective ERβ agonist LY500307 was found to reduce lung metastasis of triple-negative breast cancer cells (Zhao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: LY500307 was associated with significant increase of infiltration of neutrophils in the lung.
source: This was associated with significant increase of infiltration of neutrophils in the lung.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a previous study.

claim: The involvement of CXCR2 signalling in neutrophil infiltration has been widely reported.
source: The involvement of CXCR2 signalling in neutrophil infiltration has been widely reported.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous research.

claim: In an acute lung injury model, Cxcr2 gene deletion abolished hyperoxia-induced neutrophil accumulation.
source: In an acute lung injury model, Cxcr2 gene deletion abolished hyperoxia-induced neutrophil accumulation (Sue et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: In studies of reperfusion injury, inhibition of CXCR2 with repertaxin or anti-CXCR2 antibodies led to the reduction of neutrophils accumulation.
source: In studies of reperfusion injury, inhibition of CXCR2 with repertaxin or anti-CXCR2 antibodies led to the reduction of neutrophils accumulation (Cugini et al., 2005; Belperio et al., 2005; Bertini et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The CXCR2 antagonist SB225002 has been reported to reduce neutrophil recruitment and pro-inflammatory factor expression in LPS-induced acute lung injury.
source: The CXCR2 antagonist SB225002 has also been reported to reduce neutrophil recruitment and pro-inflammatory factor expression in LPS-induced acute lung injury (Cao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: CXCR2 signalling is a major pathway for estrogen to induce neutrophil infiltration in mammary tissue during mammary involution.
source: Using CXCR2 antagonist SB225002, this study identified CXCR2 signalling as a major pathway for estrogen to induce neutrophil infiltration in mammary tissue during mammary involution (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the CXCR2 inhibitor experiments shown in Figures 3C and 3D.

claim: The recruitment of neutrophils involves an autocrine loop, in which estrogen induces neutrophil release of CXCR2 ligands which activate CXCR2 signalling in neutrophils.
source: It is conceivable that the recruitment of neutrophils involves an autocrine loop, in which estrogen induces neutrophil release of CXCR2 ligands which activate CXCR2 signalling in neutrophils.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that estrogen upregulates both CXCR2 and its ligands in neutrophils.

claim: TREM1 was first identified to be selectively expressed on neutrophils and monocytes.
source: TREM1 was first identified to be selectively expressed on neutrophils and monocytes (Bouchon et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: TREM3 is highly homologous to TREM1 and is believed to have overlapping function.
source: TREM3 is highly homologous to TREM1 and is believed to have overlapping function.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: TREM1/3-deficient mice displayed impaired neutrophil trans-epithelial infiltration into the lung when challenged with P. aeruginosa.
source: TREM1/3-deficient mice displayed impaired neutrophil trans-epithelial infiltration into the lung when challenged with P. aeruginosa (Klesney-Tait et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: TREM1 was known to amplify inflammation, as TREM1 overactivation with activating antibodies following LPS treatment led to the up-regulation of cytokines such as TNFα, MCP-1, and IL8.
source: TREM1 was also known to amplify inflammation, as TREM1 overactivation with activating antibodies following LPS treatment led to the up-regulation of cytokines such as TNFα, MCP-1, and IL8 (Bouchon et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Trem1/3 up-regulation plays a role in estrogen-induced neutrophil infiltration.
source: It is plausible that Trem1/3 up-regulation also plays a role in estrogen-induced neutrophil infiltration.
evidence: This is speculated based on the known function of TREM1/3 and their upregulation by estrogen.

claim: Estrogen is traditionally known to promote metabolism and inhibit adipogenesis.
source: Estrogen is traditionally known to promote metabolism and inhibit adipogenesis (Chen and Brown, 1793).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: ERα signalling is required for the adipose progenitor identity and the commitment of white fat cell lineage.
source: It has been reported recently that ERα signalling is required for the adipose progenitor identity and the commitment of white fat cell lineage (Lapid et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: This study provides the first evidence that estrogen stimulates adipocytes repopulation during mammary involution.
source: The present study provides the first evidence that estrogen stimulates adipocytes repopulation during mammary involution.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding from the current study.

claim: Estrogen stimulation of adipocytes repopulation likely involved neutrophils because neutrophils depletion attenuated estrogen-induced adipocytes repopulation and the gene expression related to fat cell differentiation, lipid metabolism, and ECM remodelling.
source: This effect likely involved neutrophils because neutrophils depletion attenuated estrogen-induced adipocytes repopulation and the gene expression related to fat cell differentiation, lipid metabolism, and ECM remodelling (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the neutrophil depletion experiments.

claim: Depletion of mammary macrophage in Macrophage Fas-induced apoptosis (Mafia) transgenic mice targeting CSF1R-expressing cells resulted in delayed mammary involution and loss of LM-PCD due to attenuated activation of Stat3.
source: Depletion of mammary macrophage in Macrophage Fas-induced apoptosis (Mafia) transgenic mice targeting CSF1R-expressing cells resulted in delayed mammary involution and loss of LM-PCD due to attenuated activation of Stat3.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous research.

claim: Monocytes and macrophages played a part in estrogen-induced LM-PCD by heightening the proinflammatory tissue environment, leading to further activation of estrogen-induced lysosomal proteases.
source: Since estrogen induced monocyte recruitment and is known to regulate the transcriptional activity of macrophages (Chung et al., 2017; Pepe et al., 2017), we speculate that monocytes and macrophages played a part in estrogen-induced LM-PCD by heightening the proinflammatory tissue environment, leading to further activation of estrogen-induced lysosomal proteases.
evidence: This is speculated based on the known effects of estrogen on monocytes and macrophages.

claim: Estrogen treatment intensely and extensively regulates the activity of neutrophils to elicit inflammation and adipocytes repopulation.
source: Estrogen treatment intensely and extensively regulates the activity of neutrophils to elicit inflammation and adipocytes repopulation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: The study identified CXCR2 signalling in neutrophils as an important mechanism of estrogen-induced neutrophil recruitment.
source: The study identified CXCR2 signalling in neutrophils as an important mechanism of estrogen-induced neutrophil recruitment.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Estrogen exacerbates mammary LM-PCD by inducing the expression of Ctsb, Tnf, Bid, and subsequent lysosomal activation and leakage of CTSB, CTSD, and CTSL independent of neutrophils.
source: Additionally, estrogen also exacerbates mammary LM-PCD by inducing the expression of Ctsb, Tnf, Bid, and subsequent lysosomal activation and leakage of CTSB, CTSD, and CTSL independent of neutrophils.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Estrogen retains its function in inducing the expression of pro-growth genes to facilitate mammary regeneration for the subsequent reproduction.
source: At the same time, estrogen retains its function in inducing the expression of pro-growth genes to facilitate mammary regeneration for the subsequent reproduction.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data showing estrogen upregulation of pro-growth genes.

claim: Programmed cell death is often associated with growth, when the elimination of unwanted cells can benefit tissue remodelling and regeneration.
source: It should also be recognized that programmed cell death is often associated with growth, when the elimination of unwanted cells can benefit tissue remodelling and regeneration (Pérez-Garijo and Steller, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: In Drosophila eye imaginal discs, apoptotic cells release Spi, the EGF ligand in flies, to promote the proliferation of neighbouring cells.
source: It has been shown in Drosophila eye imaginal discs that apoptotic cells release Spi, the EGF ligand in flies, to promote the proliferation of neighbouring cells (Fan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Estrogen-induced LM-PCD during mammary involution may additionally facilitate mammary regeneration and tumor development.
source: Whether estrogen-induced LM-PCD during mammary involution additionally facilitates mammary regeneration and tumor development is an interesting area for future study.
evidence: This is proposed as a hypothesis for future investigation.

claim: E2B treatment in mice given IgG significantly increased the percentage of mammary neutrophils by 9-folds which was abolished by neutrophil depletion with Ly6G.
source: Di, E2B treatment in mice given IgG significantly increased the percentage of mammary neutrophils by 9-folds which was abolished by neutrophil depletion with Ly6G
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1Di.

claim: Estrogen promotes involution by exacerbating inflammation, cell death and adipocytes repopulation.
source: Combined analysis of transcriptomic, protein, and immunohistochemical data in BALB/c mice showed that estrogen promotes involution by exacerbating inflammation, cell death and adipocytes repopulation.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from multiple experimental approaches.

claim: E2B treatment in mice given IgG increased the percentage of mammary neutrophils by six folds and this effect was abolished by neutrophil depletion with Ly6G.
source: E2B treatment in mice given IgG increased the percentage of mammary neutrophils by six folds and this effect was abolished by neutrophil depletion with Ly6G.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Mammary monocytes was increased significantly by E2B treatment and was attenuated with Ly6G but to a non-statistically significant level.
source: Mammary monocytes was also increased significantly by E2B treatment and was attenuated with Ly6G but to a non-statistically significant level
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The relative expression of Esr1 (ERα) in mammary neutrophils during involution is approximately 40 times that of Esr2 (ERβ).
source: Firstly, the relative expression of Esr1 (ERα) in mammary neutrophils during involution is approximately 40 times that of Esr2 (ERβ) (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Estrogen reduced mammary neutrophil infiltration in age-matched nulliparous mice.
source: In sharp contrast to the effect on neutrophils during mammary involution, estrogen reduced mammary neutrophil infiltration in age-matched nulliparous mice.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Estrogen-regulated expression of cytokines such as S100a9, Cxcl2, and Cxcr2 in nulliparous mice occurs in the opposite direction as that in mice undergoing mammary involution.
source: Estrogen-regulated expression of cytokines such as S100a9, Cxcl2, and Cxcr2 in nulliparous mice also occurs in the opposite direction as that in mice undergoing mammary involution.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The observation in nulliparous mice is consistent with reports that estrogen inhibits inflammation in obesity-induced mammary inflammation, and in Staphylococcus aureus infected bovine mammary epithelial cells.
source: The observation in nulliparous mice is consistent with reports that estrogen inhibits inflammation in obesity-induced mammary inflammation (Bhardwaj et al., 2015), and in Staphylococcus aureus infected bovine mammary epithelial cells (Medina-Estrada et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: This is the first evidence of the plasticity of estrogen action on neutrophils that is shaped by the tissue microenvironment in an in vivo model.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first evidence of the plasticity of estrogen action on neutrophils that is shaped by the tissue microenvironment in an in vivo model.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding from the current study.

claim: There are fundamental differences in the cistrome of mammary neutrophils between involution and nulliparous states.
source: This suggests that there are fundamental differences in the cistrome of mammary neutrophils between these two states.
evidence: This is inferred from the opposite effects of estrogen on neutrophils in the two states.

claim: Neutrophils are known to express ERα, ERβ, and GPER30.
source: Neutrophils are known to express ERα, ERβ, and GPER30 (Molero et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: ERα and ERβ are members of the nuclear receptor superfamily of transcription factors.
source: ERα and ERβ are members of the nuclear receptor superfamily of transcription factors, whereas GPER30 is a G protein-coupled membrane receptor.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about estrogen receptors.

claim: GPER30 is a G protein-coupled membrane receptor.
source: ERα and ERβ are members of the nuclear receptor superfamily of transcription factors, whereas GPER30 is a G protein-coupled membrane receptor.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about estrogen receptors.

claim: PPT, but not DPN treatment, significantly increased mammary expression of Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Cxcl2, and Mirt2.
source: PPT, but not DPN treatment, significantly increased mammary expression of Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Cxcl2, and Mirt2 (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The regulatory effect of E2B on mammary inflammation and on neutrophil activity in particular is primarily mediated by ERα.
source: This suggests that the regulatory effect of E2B on mammary inflammation and on neutrophil activity in particular is primarily mediated by ERα.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ERα and ERβ agonist experiments.

claim: PPT, but not DPN increased the expression of adipogenesis-related genes, Ptgs2 (Cox-2), Adig, and Egr2.
source: Similar to the effect of E2B, PPT, but not DPN increased the expression of adipogenesis-related genes, Ptgs2 (Cox-2), Adig, and Egr2 (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Neither PPT nor DPN affected the expression of Cebpb.
source: However, neither PPT nor DPN affected the expression of Cebpb.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Both PPT and DPN did not affect the expression of Mmp3 but increased the expression of Mmp9.
source: Both PPT and DPN did not affect the expression of Mmp3 but increased the expression of Mmp9.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: PPT but not DPN enhanced the expression of Mmp8.
source: On the other hand, PPT but not DPN enhanced the expression of Mmp8.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: ERα is likely involved in E2B-induced adipocytes repopulation through the activity of neutrophils.
source: We deduce from these observations that ERα is likely involved in E2B-induced adipocytes repopulation through the activity of neutrophils.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ERα and ERβ agonist experiments.

claim: ERβ is known to repress the transcriptional activity of PPARγ and inhibit adipocyte differentiation.
source: It is possible that ERβ is negatively involved in the regulation of adipocytes repopulation because ERβ is known to repress the transcriptional activity of PPARγ and inhibit adipocyte differentiation (Foryst-Ludwig et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: PPT did not increase pro-CTSB.
source: Unlike the effect of E2B which also increased pro-CTSB, PPT did not seem to increase pro-CTSB.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The PPT-induced increase of pro-CTSB was already converted to the cleaved form as the pharmacodynamics of E2B and PPT are likely different.
source: We suspect that the PPT-induced increase of pro-CTSB was already converted to the cleaved form as the pharmacodynamics of E2B and PPT are likely different.
evidence: This is speculated to explain the difference between E2B and PPT effects on pro-CTSB.

claim: ERβ-specific agonist DPN did not have any effect on the gene expression of the death-inducing genes, or the activation of lysosomal proteases.
source: In contrast, ERβ-specific agonist DPN did not have any effect on the gene expression of the death-inducing genes, or the activation of lysosomal proteases (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figures 8A and 8B.

claim: ERα mediates E2B-induced LM-PCD during mammary involution.
source: These observations indicate that ERα mediates E2B-induced LM-PCD during mammary involution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ERα and ERβ agonist experiments.

claim: E2B treatment resulted in a 56.33% decrease in mammary neutrophils in nulliparous mice.
source: Flow cytometry analysis of the mammary gland showed that E2B treatment resulted in a 56.33% decrease in mammary neutrophils (CD45+ CD11b+ Gr1hi) (Figure 7A, p=0.0349).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: E2B had no significant effect on the percentage of mammary monocytes in nulliparous mice.
source: E2B had no significant effect on the percentage of mammary monocytes (CD45+ CD11b+ Ly6Chi, p=0.2965).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: E2B significantly down-regulated S100a9, Cxcl2, and Cxcr2 in nulliparous mice.
source: E2B significantly down-regulated S100a9 (p=0.0095), Cxcl2 (p=0.0382), and Cxcr2 (p=0.0236) while had no effect on the expression of S100a8, Clec4d, Il1b, and Trem3 (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: E2B had no effect on the expression of S100a8, Clec4d, Il1b, and Trem3 in nulliparous mice.
source: E2B significantly down-regulated S100a9 (p=0.0095), Cxcl2 (p=0.0382), and Cxcr2 (p=0.0236) while had no effect on the expression of S100a8, Clec4d, Il1b, and Trem3 (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: E2B up-regulated Ctsb in nulliparous mice.
source: As for the cell death-related genes, E2B up-regulated Ctsb (p=0.0166), consistent with the understanding that Ctsb is an ER target gene (Lee and Choi, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Ctsb is an ER target gene.
source: As for the cell death-related genes, E2B up-regulated Ctsb (p=0.0166), consistent with the understanding that Ctsb is an ER target gene (Lee and Choi, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: E2B had no effect on the expression of Bid in nulliparous mice.
source: However, E2B had no effect on the expression of Bid while Tnf displays no amplification in the qPCR reaction due to the low level of expression (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: E2B exerts an anti-inflammatory effect on the mammary gland of nulliparous mice.
source: Hence, unlike its effect during mammary involution, E2B exerts an anti-inflammatory effect on the mammary gland of nulliparous mice.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression data in nulliparous mice.

claim: PPT caused evidently increased the expression of Ctsb, Bid and Tnf that are known to promote cell death.
source: Similar to the effect of E2B, ERα agonist PPT evidently increased the expression of Ctsb, Bid and Tnf that are known to promote cell death (Figure 8A).
